node.title: Re^6: setting PERL_PERTURB_KEYS & PERL_HASH_SEED in a perl file
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [gravid],

Yep, there's a better solution than messing with Perl's internals :-)

my %hash = ( a=>0, b=>1, c=>0, d=>3 ); foreach my $k ( sort { $hash{$a} <=> $hash{$b} or $a cmp $b } keys %hash ) { print "$k = $hash{$k}\n"; }

Always outputs:

a = 0 c = 0 b = 1 d = 3

Background: If the comparison of the values (<=>) shows they are equal it returns zero, so then the second part of the or expression is evaluated, comparing the keys.

Update: See the multi-field sort in [doc://perlfaq4#How-do-I-sort-an-array-by-(anything)?] That FAQ answer also references this article: [http://www.perl.com/doc/FMTEYEWTK/sort.html|Far More Than Everything You've Ever Wanted to Know About Sorting]

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
